statement: For a primitive completed L-function, functional-equation routing pairs a zero rho of Lambda(s,chi) with 1-conj(rho) for the conjugate character; conjugation may also pair rho with conj(rho) when coefficients are real.

statement: Trivial zeros are routed from poles of the Gamma factor and cancellation in the completed function. For primitive Dirichlet characters, their parity controls the negative-integer progression.

examples.even_character: negative even integers, subject to standard exceptional principal cases

warning: Do not classify a zero as trivial from Re(s)<0 alone without checking the exact completed-function convention and character.

claim_gate: The taxonomy labels regions only; it proves no zero theorem.

requires: control of poles and trivial zeros
rejects: finite zero table implies explicit formula
formal contour shift without boundary bounds

forward: A zero can be attached as global spectral metadata to an ANT object whose local prime-axis coefficients are represented in PVG.
reverse: Prime-axis valuation data alone do not reconstruct analytic continuation, Gamma factors, or zero locations.
preserves: link from Euler coefficients to global analytic object
